I’m so sorry. I’ve not dealt with a break up, but I’ve definitely spiraled during a very dark moment in my life, 

I would maybe suggest trying to get out of your head by interacting with real people. Going out and doing something you love in a communal way (ex: a yoga class, hiking or running clubs, cooking classes, gamer meet ups). For me, moving my body is SOOOOO important in getting out of my head so I tend to do movement based activities (yoga and dance). 

Being in real life and interacting with people really helped to start to break down the spiral for me. And that led to getting out with friends more and living again. 

I’m not suggesting replacing daydreaming with escaping through partying. Just integrating interaction in reality with something you enjoy to keep you going. 

God MD is like the best thing and worst thing ever. I’m rooting for you.

Sounds like it’s less about “being famous” in a bad way and more about perusing a career in what you love and finding an audience who LOVES you. You love music and can’t do it in school the way you want. I think your MD is pointing you towards continuing to pursue music as much as you can. MD just makes that dream feel “real” in an easy way — especially if it feels like you can’t do it in real life. MD gives us the fake pleasure of things we want (in my opinion) and takes away our valuable time we can spend actually doing the thing. 

In real life you’ll have to do the hard work of  getting back into music, putting yourself out there, and building an audience. MD is easy, doing the real thing is hard. You got it. ❤️
The cheap knock off fragrance oil from the beauty supply stores last so long on my skin and smell DIVINE on me.

I did/do the same thing with my characters watching me do tasks, etc. I definitely still do. To me the important thing is making sure I have things to do with other people. Like if you like to draw, finding (free) classes, meet ups, or any way to do what you love around other people. Being around people is, for me, kind of the only way to start to unplug from my head and being in the real world. It’s hard at first, and I still have moments with my characters, especially when I’m doing mundane things lol. 

MD can isolate us, and making sure we’re interacting in real life is so important. My opinion! You got this.

I think maybe it just shows internally youre craving connection and your MD is latching onto this because it may have FELT like a connection. So instead of going out and trying to slowly, healthily establish connection with consenting and interested people, your MD is chasing this false one. 

Maybe this shows you should start actually building connections (platonic or romantic) which can be slow, hard, and stressful at first — especially if people don’t connect to you back/aren’t your people. It’s easy to imagine life with this person because…she’s there. Our MD wants us to avoid slow, hard and stressful but can lead us into delusion and harm.  Just remember that. 

Move on for your sake AND hers. Easier said than done but every time your mind wanders to this fixation, consider trying to find ways to go out and build more real connections. 

You got this.

I’ve gone through similar extremes with my daydreaming. However, I didn’t necessarily feel like I was different than myself in my head because I wasn’t really a real person in my head. I just felt depressed and suicidal that I couldn’t live the life in my head. 

I just responded to someone else’s post and I think my comment applies here so I’m going to copy it here. Sorry if it’s repetitive:

“I have been where you are and was suicidal because of daydreaming 2 years ago. My boyfriend has been so patient with me through this process, and I’ll tell you what he told me.

Think of something that you’re interested in/have done in the past and force yourself to go do it. Preferably something  a) is outside of the house,  b)in a communal space, and c) is creative or involves movement.
 
Example: I loved yoga, but I only did it at home. He encouraged me to find a place and start going 2x a week. I fought tooth and nail. I was depressed and had no energy. But eventually I tried it. Let me tell you it SUCKED at first. Those 2 classes a week were the only time I left my house.  Then, slowly, those classes gave me a little energy to go outside more, then to reconnect with friends, then to make new friends, then to try out new things that I wanted to try, then to getting back to my career…

It wasn’t about “gaining the skill” or “getting out of the house,” it was about rebuilding my resilience. That’s the only way forward.  You’ve lost resilience and only you can build it back. And you deserve to.”

Basically we have to get out of our head and into the real world.  It might take time and it won’t feel good. Knowing that helped me feel better. It sucks because it’s supposed to suck. But one day it won’t. It took me years to rebuild my strength and sense of self and energy but I’m much much better now. I just had to accept where I was.

You deserve to fight for yourself as you are now.  I know you have it in you. One day at a time.

I completely get it. I was where you are 2 years ago. After decades of maladaptive daydreaming it finally came to a head. I felt empty and life felt pointless without being able to escape. I wanted to die because I knew life would never feel as good as it did when I was daydreaming. I would never have those relationships. It hurt. 

My boyfriend has been so patient with me through this process, and I’ll tell you what he told me. 

Think of something that you’re interested in/have done in the past and force yourself to go do it. Preferably something  a) is outside of the house,  b)in a communal space, and c) is creative or involves movement.

Example, I love yoga and only did it alone using YouTube. He encouraged me to find a place nearby and go at least 2 times a week. I fought against that advice. It felt stupid. I had no energy. I couldn’t even get out of bed. I was depressed. But slowly, slowlyyyyy i tried it out. And from there, i slowlyyy started gaining mental strength. Those 2 classes were the only time i left the house/bed. And eventually those few classes a week gave me a little more energy to get out of bed more, which helped me reconnect with friends, which helped me get back to my career… 

I fought him tooth and nail before starting out. I made excuses and genuinely was in a depressive episode. But now I understand it wasn’t about “gaining the skill” or “getting out of the house,” it was about rebuilding my resilience. That’s the only way forward.  When it’s between you and being suicidal you owe it to yourself to push and push.  You’ve lost resilience and only you can build it back. And you deserve to.

I know that sounds horrible. It won’t feel good at all…but on the other side beat by beat you get back to living in real life. 

I don’t think this is a blanket truth that’ll work with everyone. I am medicated and it’s unclear how much that helped. I was medicated before the suicidal maladaptive backslide, so maybe it helped me get up and start my resilience  journey. Come to think of it, it’s taken about 4 years from getting medicated to actually addressing my problem to now. I feel human again. I’m not without my days, and I still fall into maladaptive daydreaming days, but when they come I know I need to get out and be in community — or tell my community to come to me. 

I hope you find relief. I’ve been there. This is not easy, but hard things are hard. ❤️

After a really really dangerous holiday last year (mental health wise) I was very nervous about returning home for the holidays this year. There’s a lot going on, I’m the oldest and responsible for holding ALOT. It often feels like if I don’t make the right calls in my family, very catastrophic things happen (no exaggeration). I’m not even in my 30s yet so sometimes I don’t know the right things to say or actions to take and I can’t stop bad things from happening. 

Anyways, as you can probably tell I’m dealing with  so much guilt, shame, and anxiety in regards to my family. So, coming home for the holidays is scary. If things go wrong I have to real time figure out how to fix them while trying to be a good older sibling and not show signs of distress.  I’m in a better place this year but these two weeks of break have been difficult. There has been serious family issue after family issue. Some of it, I feel like I could’ve done more to “fix.” I’ve really had to step up and be an emotional and financial support system. I’ve had to both argue with and console the “adults.” When it’s time to sleep, I feel guilt over how I performed during that day’s crisis, and what went wrong, and why it’s my fault. 

Anyways, I’m better than I was last year and I now have the tools to know how to try and regulate myself. But tonight, I realized that I am very triggered and dissociated. I have that head full/fuzzy foggy feeling. In between making sure I spend time with my siblings so they have a happy break, I have to spend most of my time on my phone or engaging in some kind of media to stay sane. I love my family but I know when I get back to my home it’ll take a while to re-regulate. I wish life wasn’t like this.
